key_insight: Detonation-sprayed hydroxyapatite coatings improved Grade 2 titanium wear resistance, with the best friction and wear performance at O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 3.0 and 3.3.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing the spray gas ratio could improve the durability of titanium implant surfaces under physiological lubrication.
method: Deposit hydroxyapatite on Grade 2 titanium at O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 2.6–3.7.
Identify coating phases using X-ray diffraction.
Evaluate friction and wear under dry conditions and in Ringer’s solution.
evidence_signal: Tribological tests showed higher wear resistance than uncoated titanium, while X-ray diffraction identified predominantly hydroxyapatite with partial α-tricalcium phosphate formation.
watch_item: Improved osseointegration and long-term implant reliability remain unverified by the biological and durability evidence reported in the abstract.
paper_title: STUDY OF TRIBOLOGICAL PROPERTIES OF BIOCOATINGS BY DETONATION SPRAYING METHOD
